result.topic_en: Scholion 3 sets φ = π/2 to express (π/2)∫xⁿdx(1−x)ⁿ⁻¹ by series and imaginary binomials, then removes the imaginaries with t = tan ω to obtain a double-integral formula in a real angle θ; Example 3 on interrupted arithmetic progressions of arcs begins at the foot of the page.

176

Scholion 3.

§. 24. Ponamus in genere $\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$, eritque
$\sin. n\phi = \sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}$; $\sin. (n+1)\phi = \cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}$;
$\sin. (n+2)\phi = -\sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}$; $\sin. (n+3)\phi = -\cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}$; etc.
Vnde resultat haec aequatio:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{2}[?]\sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}\left(\frac{1}{nn} - \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2(n+2)^2} + \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)(2n+3)}{1.2.3.4(n+4)^2} - \text{etc.}\right)$
$- \cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}\left(\frac{2n}{1(n+1)^2} - \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1.2.3(n+3)^2} + \text{etc.}\right)$
At ex superiori reductione manifestum est fore:
$1 - \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1.2}t^2 + \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)(2n+3)}{1.2.3.4}t^4 - \text{etc.}$
$= \frac{(1+t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n} + (1-t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n}}{2}$,
$\frac{2n}{1}t - \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1.2.3}t^3 + \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)(2n+3)(2n+4)}{1.2.3.4.5}t^5 - \text{etc.}$
$= \frac{(1+t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n} - (1-t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n}}{2\sqrt{-1}}$,
hincque colligitur:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{2}\sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1+t\sqrt{-1})^{2n}}$
$+ \frac{1}{2}\sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1-t\sqrt{-1})^{2n}}$
$- \frac{1}{2\sqrt{-1}}\cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1+t\sqrt{-1})^{2n}}$
$+ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{-1}}\cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t}\int\frac{t^{n-1}dt}{(1-t\sqrt{-1})^{2n}}$,
vbi quidem post integrationem poni oportet $t = 1$. Vt autem hanc expressionem ab imaginariis liberemus ponamus:
$t =$

$t = \text{tang.}\, \omega = \frac{\sin. \omega}{\cos. \omega}$, erit $dt = \frac{d\omega}{\cos. \omega^2}$; $\frac{dt}{t} = \frac{d\omega}{\sin. \omega \cos. \omega}$;
$t^{n-1}dt = \frac{d\omega \sin. \omega^{n-1}}{\cos. \omega^{n+1}}$,
tum vero
$(1+t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n} = \cos. \omega^{2n}(\cos. \omega + \sqrt{-1}.\sin. \omega)^{-2n}$
$= \cos. \omega^{2n}(\cos. 2n\omega - \sqrt{-1}.\sin. 2n\omega)$
$(1-t\sqrt{-1})^{-2n} = \cos. \omega^{2n}(\cos. \omega - \sqrt{-1}.\sin. \omega)^{-2n}$
$= \cos. \omega^{2n}(\cos. 2n\omega + \sqrt{-1}.\sin. 2n\omega)$.
Quibus valoribus substitutis imaginaria se mutuo tollent, prodibitque haec aequatio:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \sin. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{d\omega}{\sin. \omega \cos. \omega}\int d\omega \sin. \omega^{n-1}\cos. \omega^{n-1}\cos. 2n\omega$
$+ \cos. \frac{n\pi}{2}\int\frac{d\omega}{\sin. \omega \cos. \omega}\int d\omega \sin. \omega^{n-1}\cos. \omega^{n-1}\sin. 2n\omega$
quae in hanc simpliciorem contrahitur:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \int\frac{d\omega}{\sin. \omega \cos. \omega}\int d\omega \sin. \omega^{n-1}\cos. \omega^{n-1}\sin. (\frac{n\pi}{2} + 2n\omega)$
vel, ob $\sin. \omega \cos. \omega = \frac{1}{2}\sin. 2\omega$, in hanc:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{2^n}\int\frac{2d\omega}{\sin. 2\omega}\int 2d\omega \sin. 2\omega^{n-1}\sin. (\frac{n\pi}{2} + 2n\omega)$.
Sit nunc angulus $2\omega = \theta$, vt fiat concinnius:
$\frac{\pi}{2}\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{2^n}\int\frac{d\theta}{\sin. \theta}\int d\theta \sin. \theta^{n-1}\sin. n(\frac{\pi}{2} + \theta)$
vbi post integrationem statui oportet $\theta = 90^\circ = \frac{\pi}{2}$. Vt tum fiat $\omega = 45^\circ$ et $t = \cos. \omega = 1$.
